notes.D9-05: verified and UNDERSTATED by the finder: longest GIL hold 265-412 ms (reported 39.4), p99 232-338 ms (reported 35.8), across the quiet window and two independent verifiers; stage attribution is dhw_lp_build / scalar_sim, not simulate_trajectory_batch. An ordinary Python thread starves as badly as the loop (0.939 share, 403 ms), so this is whole-interpreter GIL starvation - in real HA the recorder thread and every other integration's executor job stop too. That settles the fix in favour of the process route; note coordinator.py:4735 passes a LAMBDA to the executor, so ProcessPoolExecutor needs the call restructured first, and the fix names neither the what-if solve (:10776) nor diagnose_last_interval (:10104). It is GIL hand-off convoy, which also explains why a CONTENDED box showed SMALLER maxima. Cheap mitigation measured: a 10x shorter switch interval takes the longest hold 409 -> 4.6 ms and the share 0.951 -> 0 for +3 % CPU.
